name: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd
about: Tata Consultancy Services is the flagship company and a part of Tata group. It is an IT services, consulting and business solutions organization that has been partnering with many of the world's largest businesses in their transformation journeys for over 50 years. TCS offers a consulting-led, cognitive powered, integrated portfolio of business, technology and engineering services and solutions. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 10.2% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 8.7%.
EBITDA margin compressed 130 bps over 5 years (28.4% → 27.1%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 5% to 11% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 25.7%, 160 bps below a year ago.
Over 5 years: ₹225,102 cr of profit, ₹227,254 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.01x.

ledger.quote: Overall, our long-term aspiration remains unchanged, continues to be 26% to 28%.
ledger.speaker: Samir Seksaria
ledger.evidence: Q2 FY27 operating margin was 24% (C1), 200bps below the 26% floor. On the facts' margin basis it is 25.7%, down from 27.3% a year earlier (F:margin_last_q_pct, F:margin_same_q_last_year_pct). Management is putting investment (bench, subcontractors, M&A) ahead of margin (C1). No date is attached to the aspiration.

ledger.quote: target to have at least 1% of our employee base, to work in the new operating model
ledger.statement: Target at least 1% of employees working in the new (FDE) operating model
ledger.speaker: Aarthi Subramanian
ledger.evidence: No headcount or FDE-model figures are in the inputs.

ledger.quote: to progressively inch up closer, at least to the FY26 levels
ledger.statement: Progressively move operating margin back toward at least FY26 levels while reinvesting
ledger.speaker: Samir Seksaria
ledger.evidence: Q2 FY27 operating margin was flat sequentially at 24% (C1). The facts' margin is 25.7% in both Q1 and Q2 FY27, against 27.2-27.3% in H2 FY26 (F:margin_last4_pct). There is no progress yet, and Q2 was partly propped up by currency gains (C1).

ledger.quote: On the wage increments, you should expect a similar impact on what we have seen in the past annual increment cycle, which had been in the range of 150 to 200 basis points.
ledger.statement: Next annual wage increment to weigh on margins by a similar 150-200 bps as in past cycles
ledger.speaker: Samir Seksaria
ledger.evidence: The inputs don't say when the increment took effect. The facts' margin fell 160bps sequentially in Q1 FY27, from 27.3% to 25.7% (F:margin_last4_pct), inside the 150-200bps band, but C1 also cites bench and subcontractor costs, so the wage effect can't be isolated.

ledger.quote: our attempt would be to ensure that we arrest the degrowth while the AI revenue increase
ledger.statement: Aim to arrest revenue degrowth in the initial AI year while AI revenue rises
ledger.speaker: K Krithivasan
ledger.evidence: Constant-currency revenue grew 2.8% YoY and 0.5% QoQ in Q2 FY27 (C1), so revenue is not shrinking. AI revenue is not sized in the inputs.

ledger.quote: We expect the ongoing impact to be minimal, around 10 to 15 basis points.
ledger.statement: Ongoing labour code impact of about 10-15 bps
ledger.speaker: Samir Seksaria
ledger.evidence: The labour-code cost is not broken out in the inputs.

ledger.quote: we will be somewhere closer to about US$38- 39 billion for the year
ledger.statement: Order book of about USD38-39 billion for FY26 if the current trend continues
ledger.speaker: K Krithivasan
ledger.evidence: FY26 has ended, but the FY26 order book (TCV) is not in the inputs.

ledger.quote: We are taking every step to ensure that we grow better than FY '25 in FY '26 in the international market.
ledger.statement: International revenue to grow better than FY25 levels in FY26
ledger.speaker: K Krithivasan
ledger.evidence: FY26 has ended, but international revenue growth for FY25 and FY26 is not in the inputs.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Reiterates the 26-28% long-term margin aspiration as unchanged, while conceding weak regional-market revenue in Q2.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says it remains confident in converting demand into stronger growth and that its aspiration is to progressively restore margins toward FY26 levels, despite a 130 bps sequential margin decline.

tones.label: cautious
tones.why: Flags wage-increment headwinds and aims only to arrest degrowth, while stressing margin discipline.

tones.label: confident

context.speaker: Samir Seksaria
context.text: Thank you, Krithi. Good day everyone. Our quarterly revenue was ₹73,188 crore, a growth of 1.3% sequentially and 11.2% on a year-on-year basis. In dollar terms, revenue was $7,642 million, a growth of 20 basis points sequentially and 2.4% year-on-year. Page 3 of 28 In constant currency terms, our growth was 50 basis points QoQ and 2.8% YoY. Our operating margins remained stable sequentially at 24%. Consistent with our philosophy to drive long-term profitable growth, we continued to prioritize investments for growth. In Q2, we made investments in strategic partnerships, M&A-related initiatives, and hiring of niche talent. As we build future capacity and navigate demand transitions, we have invested in a higher bench and increased hiring of subcontractors to meet near-term skills and delivery requirements. This quarter, we were able to mitigate these headwinds partly by currency gains and operating leverage. Many of these investments are strategic in nature and are focused on long- term value creation. Our disciplined approach to margin management remains unchanged. context.speaker: Our priority remains clear
context.text: convert investments into sustainable growth while preserving the discipline that has consistently underpinned our profitability. Our net margins for the quarter were 19%. DSO stood at 74 days, constant sequentially in dollar terms. Our cash conversion remains strong at 102.2% of net income and funds invested at the end of the period stood at $5.98 billion. Our capital allocation policy remains unchanged, and we remain committed to returning substantial free cash flows to our shareholders while judiciously investing to support our long-term growth aspirations. I will now hand it over to Aarthi.

context.speaker: Our priority is clear
context.text: use AI to create measurable value for our customers, and to improve how we deliver work for them. This quarter, we made Page 5 of 28 progress on both fronts, with growth in our AI business and wider adoption of our Human+AI services delivery model. We are seeing three distinct demand patterns: (1) AI-native solutions with business outcomes, (2) AI-led transformation of enterprise systems, and (3) Autonomous GBS. Enterprises are also prioritizing investments in modernizing legacy data estates and building AI-ready data foundations. Across these demand patterns, strong AI governance with secure AI platforms is becoming a top need for enterprises. Let me share an example of how we are building AI-native solutions with assured business outcomes.  For a global industrial manufacturer, we are using an AI-native approach to solve a critical business need, compressing lead-to- quote time from 4.7 days to under an hour. We achieved this within a quarter, clearly demonstrating speed to value. The next step is to improve their lead-to-conversion metric. This is a good example of focused problem-solving and business outcome realization with AI. Now let me share how AI is changing the approach to transforming enterprise systems. AI is playing a key role in process mining, which helps us understand existing workflows. Redesigning processes with a human and AI approach by default is enabling upfront identification of agentic opportunities. And the acceleration of implementations with AI is real.  In a large, complex S/4HANA enterprise transformation spanning 27 sites, more than 70 legal entities, we are using AI to redesign processes and accelerate implementation. credibility.label: medium
credibility.summary: Most of TCS's guidance is undated aspiration (a 26-28% margin, inching back to FY26 margins, arresting degrowth) that the inputs can't close out. What can be tested shows operating margin parked at 24%, 200bps below the aspiration floor, and constant-currency growth of 2.8% behind an 11.2% rupee headline.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Q2 revenue of INR73,188 crore, up 11.2% YoY (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Constant-currency growth was 2.8% YoY and USD growth 2.4%, so about 8.4 points of the rupee growth came from currency. The 3-year rupee revenue CAGR is 5.8%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Management says its 'disciplined approach to margin management remains unchanged', and the 26-28% aspiration stands (C1, G1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Operating margin is 24%. The facts' margin is 25.7% against 27.3% a year earlier and has been flat for two quarters, with a 5-year change of -130bps. Currency gains helped Q2.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Cash conversion of 102.2% of net income (C2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: 5-year CFO/PAT is 1.01 and 5-year FCF INR2,10,402 crore. CCC has drifted to 93 days from 81, with DSO at 74 days.

bull.point: Cash generation: 5-year FCF is INR2,10,402 crore, CFO/PAT 1.01, Q2 cash conversion 102.2%, ROCE 63% and D/E 0.1.
Revenue has stopped shrinking: constant currency grew 2.8% YoY and 0.5% QoQ, in line with the aim to arrest degrowth. Rupee growth ran 4.9%, 9.6%, 13.9% and 11.2% over the last four quarters.
Profit is still growing: Q2 FY27 PAT rose 14.9% YoY at a 19% net margin, and operating margin held at 24% QoQ despite investment in bench and M&A.

bear.point: Underlying growth is thin: USD revenue rose 2.4% and constant currency 2.8% YoY, and the 3-year revenue and PAT CAGRs are 5.8% and 5.3%.

Margin is below the stated band and drifting: operating margin is 24% against the 26-28% aspiration, and the facts' margin 25.7% against 27.3% a year ago. Each wage cycle costs 150-200bps, and Q2 was helped by currency gains that can reverse.
Working capital is lengthening: CCC is 93 days against 81 three years ago, and DSO is 74 days.

questions: Excluding currency gains, what was Q2 FY27 operating margin, and when do you expect to be back inside 26-28% given the higher bench and subcontractor use? PAT grew 14.9% while margin fell 160bps YoY: what below-the-line items drove that?
What were the FY26 order book, against the USD38-39 billion indication, and FY26 international growth versus FY25?
How large is AI revenue today, how much legacy revenue is it cannibalising, and what share of employees is in the new FDE model against the 1% target?
